Visual references (Lucas sent eleven images as mood references; they are described here in words. Some are film stills or photos of real people: they set a look and a tone only, and no character is based on anyone's face.)

**01 · Bar, close two-shot** (`01-bar-close-two-shot.jpg`). A dim, crowded dive bar at night.
Two people pressed close in the foreground: she faces camera-left with a wary look; he stands
right behind her, chin near her shoulder, looking past her. Their faces are lit low and warm
from the side, skin with a soft sheen, and everything else sinks into brown-black. Behind them:
amber wall sconces, a red neon strip, a cold green glow from a drinks fridge, small red points
of light along the bar, all soft in shallow focus. Intimacy that reads as threat.

**02 · Candlelit bar counter** (`02-candlelit-bar-counter.jpg`). A cramped bar lit by vintage
lamps: a green glass lantern, a red fringed shade, candles in glasses on the counter among the
bottles, a chalkboard menu behind. Heavy red and green colour, black corners, film grain and a
vignette, like an old snapshot. A couple sits close at the end of the bar, her in a white top,
him leaning in.

**03 · Record bar** (`03-record-bar.jpg`). A listening bar: a floor-to-ceiling wall of vinyl
records behind the bar, warm dome pendant lamps hung low, rows of bottles, backlit hi-fi
units. Patrons in silhouette; a man and a woman seated side by side at the bar, seen from
behind. Warm amber, mostly shadow.

**04 · Doubled portrait** (`04-doubled-portrait.jpg`). A pale woman with long auburn hair
stares into the lens, flat and cold, against black; a blurred second copy of her turns away
beside her, like a double exposure. A self split in two.

**05 · Bathtub, black and white** (`05-bathtub-bw.jpg`). A black-and-white photo in a tiled
bathroom. A young woman in a polka-dot blouse, an apron and rubber gloves holds up the head of
a charred, blood-slick body slumped in the tub, and smiles at the camera as if posing for a
family snapshot. Domestic calm and neatness right next to horror: she is pleasant, the scene
is monstrous.

**06 · The morning after** (`06-morning-after.jpg`). A warm, yellow-tinged snapshot taken from
the pillows, like a phone photo with the flash on. A man with long locs and a tattooed arm sleeps
face-down into the pillow, mouth open; the woman beside him is awake, a hand pressed to her
forehead, staring off, bored and uneasy. Soft focus, crumpled patterned bedding. He is out cold;
she is somewhere else in her head.

**07 · The abandoned hotel inside** (`07-abandoned-hotel-interior.jpg`). Inside an old,
abandoned hotel: a carved-leg pool table in the middle of a bare plank floor, a tall rack of
cues, a wood stove, a long table with spindle chairs, pressed-tin walls, an open white door.
Low sun slants through tall windows and throws lace-like patterns of light across the wall and
floor; everything else is dust-brown shadow, sepia and still, untouched for decades.

**08 · The desert motel** (`08-desert-motel.jpg`). An abandoned roadside motel in flat desert:
a big peeling "MOTEL" sign on steel legs with a red "OFFICE" arrow, a gutted two-storey block, a
long carport, palm trees and dry scrub in front, a pale washed-out sky, dusty faded-film colour.

**09 · The joy ride** (`09-joy-ride.jpg`). A vintage silver open two-seater convertible, 1950s
shape, seen from behind on a winding mountain road at sunset above a sea of cloud; the low sun
flares from the left, the light gold and warm; two people in the seats. The romantic, free
version of the drive, which the cold open plays against.

**10 · Two faces, sepia** (`10-two-faces-sepia.jpg`). A sepia portrait: a woman's composed face
in front, three-quarter to camera, chin resting on her hand, calm and pleasant. Behind her, a
second version of her face, half in shadow, stares straight into the lens with dark streaks
running down from the eye like black tears. The monster behind the composure.

**11 · The open road** (`11-open-road.jpg`). An aerial of a red vintage open-top sports car,
alone on a straight two-lane road through golden grassland at sunset. Hazy, warm, low light;
the grass moves in the wind; hills far off in the haze. Wide, lonely and golden.

development.logline: A vigilante who falls in love with every unpunished man she sentences drives her latest across the desert, laughing and filming him, still waiting for the dead man to love her back.
development.premise: Laughing, Venus drives through an empty desert town, filming the man asleep beside her, until his pale, open eyes show he is dead. At an abandoned motel, pistol in her back pocket, she unloads the luggage into the room she has kept for weeks: walls of Jean photos, none of them together. Flashback: a Thursday dive bar, Jean three nights drunk over a breakup, a stranger asking "have we met before?" She has watched him for months; his ex's domestic-violence report went nowhere. Her game, decorum, is her verdict: each lie costs him a straw. In her all-white apartment Jean wipes dried blood off the toilet; her meds sit untaken; a trance-soul track quiets her. She slides over her metal tin and asks for one true thing about love, his last straw; he gives her a line, and she opens it. By morning the "trip" has stopped his heart; she lies awake beside him, waiting for him to turn over, then remakes the white bed until it is spotless. At the motel she seats Jean at the table, takes the first photograph of them together, and pins it beside the first photos of the next man.
what_makes_it_specific: Kept: Lucas's cold open as he wrote it. The laughing joy ride with a man who seems asleep, the reveal of his pale, lost eyes, the pistol, the motel she keeps, and the wall of photos 'yet none of them together'.

Kept: the decorum straw game and its dialogue, the names Venus and St. Jean ('J'), the all-white apartment with Jean in black as her black hole, the dried blood he wipes away, the untaken meds, the aftermath of the night, and the female-Dexter engine of luring unpunished men over a date.
Obvious version: a gender-swapped Dexter. A cool, in-control vigilante seduces a predator, the last scene reveals she is the killer, and a voiceover lays out her code.

Differs by what it costs her: Venus is not in control. She is in limerence with every man she condemns, and killing him is the only way he can never leave her. The pilot opens after the kill, so the suspense is why she still loves him, not whether she will do it. The cost shows on screen: the tin stays closed until his line about love, because she was hoping he would pass (A18).
Added detail (A04): decorum is her private verdict. She already knows the true answers, and each lie Jean tells takes a straw off the house. His line about love costs him the last straw.
Added ending (A06): the first photograph of the two of them together, pinned beside the next man's photos. It pays off Lucas's 'none of them together' and shows the series engine in one frame.
Added payoff: Venus's 'let's take a trip' comes true twice, first as the tin and then as the road trip with his body.
Added season question (A17): the one man who passes decorum. The pilot's pattern of one lie, one straw and one sentence exists so that a later episode can break it.
Product role: none. This is an unbranded original drama with nothing to sell, so there is no product to become decoration.

Taste notes: every one is followed and none is broken. Following 'Hands before faces', Jean's face is held back until the dead-eyes reveal. Following 'Sound design before music', the only music plays inside the scene. Following 'Restraint over explanation', her meds are seen but never named as the reason. 'The product is a tool, then a hero' does not apply because there is no product.

strategy.proposition: Punishing the man the system lost can't make him love her back.
strategy.tension:
Viewer (who the show is for): people who follow true-crime cases online, on the night a case they have followed for months closes with nobody charged and they keep reading anyway [brief.audience; the moment is H1]. In their voice: I want the man who walked to be punished, yet months later I still look him up, waiting for a confession he will never give me. [H1] The loss they'd hate to admit: the man they want punished now has more of their attention than the person he hurt, and wanting justice has turned into a one-sided attachment that no verdict would end. The referent is the man who walked, which makes the viewer a direct mirror of Venus: she falls for the man she sentences, carries out the sentence herself, and still waits for him to love her back. Take the show away and the tension still exists. Viewer proxy (assumption, used only if V02 or S03 go public): followers of true-crime podcasts, forums and creator channels. Rejected drafts: H7 (guilt at cheering for a killer) and H10 (attachment to the victim, not to him).

Buyer (who acts): drama development execs at streamers and networks, at the point where they sort genre pitches into the few they take to script [brief.audience]. Proxy (assumption): a named list the producer or agent emails a private screener link to. There is no media buy. Execs buy when they believe this viewer exists. Their own conflict, a hook this audience already binges against the fear of buying a copy, is the Barrier and not the tension [H2, H8].

V01 cold open, 90 s, 16:9. Keeps: the drive, filming, the eyes, pistol, untouched motel, unloading and the wall. It moves decorum into the cold open with no words (question for Lucas) and leaves the last straw standing for D01. Look: hand-matched hard cuts between the candlelit bar and the hard-sun desert; straws on wood and wind; no score.
0-4 s [G]: the bar at night. Two pairs of hands lay the first straws on the bar top as a floor plan; a glass is set down; laughter, no words.
4-10 s [G]: the desert, close across the seats. A bent bar straw sits in his black shirt pocket; his head is turned to the door; she films him 'asleep', laughing.
10-16 s [G]: the bar. His hand adds a straw and the house gets a wall; her hand rests on his forearm.
16-22 s [G]: an empty desert town slides past; she straightens his collar.
22-30 s [G, hand risky; fallback G, the house already smaller, no pull shown]: the bar. His hand turns his glass; her hand pauses over the house, then draws one straw out. He drinks.
30-36 s [G]: the desert. A bump rocks his head against the door; she sets the phone in her lap, rights his head and picks the phone back up.
36-44 s [G]: the bar. Two more straws come out; the house is down to one wall.
44-50 s [G, hand risky; fallback G, the straw already back in the pocket, her hand leaving]: the desert. The wind lifts the bent straw half out of his pocket; her hand presses it back in.
50-54 s [G]: the bar. One straw still standing. Her fingertip rests on it and doesn't pull; the room's murmur drops away.
54-62 s [G, first try in the moving car (A16); fallback G, parked]: hard cut to his open, pale eyes behind slipped sunglasses; they don't blink in the wind. Her face for the first time, laughing as she pushes the glasses back up.
62-70 s [G, hand risky; fallback G, pistol visible, no hand]: the MOTEL sign. Pistol in her back pocket, she checks the padlock and the unbroken dust on the office step.
70-76 s [G]: she takes the bent straw from his pocket, then unloads the bags and groceries.
76-86 s [G]: the room. Groceries on the table with the bent straw laid beside them; the wall of photos of him, none of them together.
86-90 s [C]: LIMERENCE on the final frame, silent.
Shortest cut (V02, 15 s, 9:16, muted): 0-1.5 s the bar, her hand draws a straw out and a wall of the house drops; 1.5-4 s her phone records him asleep, the straw in his pocket; 4-6 s the bar, another straw out; 6-8 s one straw standing, her fingertip resting on it; 8-11 s his open, unblinking eyes; 11-13 s her face, laughing, pushes his glasses back up; 13-15 s LIMERENCE card.
Stills: S03 becomes the route's poster frame; S01 has the bent straw in his pocket.
Recurring device: the straw house, rebuilt with each man. The season question is the house that stands (A17).
CTA: none. The exec should open D01 and request the pilot script.

data.recommendation:
Proposition: 'Punishing the man the system lost can't make him love her back.' Proof beat, 50-56 s: after his open eyes the phone comes back up, REC 01:04:55, her thumb rests on the flip-camera icon, then slides back; the lens stays on him. 18-26 s plants the same pause before the eyes, so after them it reads as 'not like this, not yet'. Success: at least 3 of 5 development readers say unprompted, after the 90 s V01, that it's about her wanting him to love her back; V02's post-eyes flip beat (11-13 s) serves the 4-of-5 muted read.
Gives up: the objective camera for most of the drive, Venus's face until 34 s, Jean's until 42 s, and full screen width for 40 of 90 s (0-34 s and 50-56 s).
Failure: at 18-26 s and 50-56 s the thumb on the icon is too small to read at phone size, and thumbs garble in generation. Fix: the C fallback keeps the choice: the screen flips to the front camera for under a second, catches both of them (his head slumped away at 18-26 s; his open eyes aimed past the lens at 50-56 s), then flips back to him. At 42-50 s (A16) the open eyes in a moving car may not hold; the fallback moves the reveal to the parked car at the motel.
Kill test: in the H2 test, fewer than 3 of 5 readers say after V01 that it's about her wanting him to love her back, and they read the phone as trophy-taking or as her keeping herself out of frame with a body. Then the photograph idea has failed, not the craft. Switch to R1, whose unreturned squeeze carries the want with no camera.
Case R1: tone ('Tender... Her laugh, her phone and her hands fixing his collar carry it') and the V01 label as written. Pick R1 if Lucas wants the drive in the objective camera with her face in the first act, or if the phone frame tests as a gimmick.
Case R3: the D01 label's season question (A17, the one man who tells the truth at decorum), read with H5. Pick R3 if readers say the engine pages (F19: new man, new decorum, new wall) decide a script request, because only R3 puts decorum in the cold open. Lucas must also accept V01 spending the bar flashback.

lenses.verdict: Not for production today. This is the most distinctive package this idea could get. The phone-versus-film rule answers Lucas's 35mm direction with a reason, and every department serves the route: her shadow on him, her head inside one of his prints, the front camera used once per man. It is not yet a single document a crew can shoot from. Three contradictions will stop the floor on day one, and one of them nobody has flagged: the sound plan's D01 music grid runs about 10 s off the treatment and at a different tempo. The other two are where Jean's sunglasses are at the bar and whether the motel door is open or shut. The director still hasn't ruled on which way the phone screen faces, which blocks three hero plates. V02's hero punch-in fails its own check at 720p. V02 also ends on a title over black, an unflagged break of the taste notes. Every consent, price and capability is still open. Make the 20 notes and get Lucas's answers on the proposition, A02, S01 and heritage. At that point this is an A, and I would put it in front of a commissioner.

script.idea_in_one_line: She laughs and films a sleeping man across the desert until his open eyes show he is dead, then sets a table for two under a wall of his photos, none of them together.

beats.picture: Inside her phone's upright frame, centered in black: JEAN sits in the passenger seat of an open two-seater, cheek on the headrest, head turned to the door, so only his black collar, jaw and one arm of his sunglasses show. Low gold sun; the edge of an empty town slides by behind him. The picture jolts when she laughs.
beats.sound: Wind clipping the phone mic. VENUS's laugh, loud and right on the mic. No score.

beats.picture: Phone frame. The car rolls to a full stop at a stop sign on an empty crossroads, with no other car in any direction and the sign behind his head. VENUS's free hand enters the frame, brushes dust off his black shirt and straightens his collar. He doesn't stir. The frame lurches as she drives on. [Fallback: her hand only rests on his collar.]
beats.sound: The engine idling, the wind dropped to nothing, her fingers brushing fabric close to the mic, then the engine pulling away.

beats.picture: Three jump cuts inside the phone frame, the timer jumping at each: empty storefronts, then open desert, then scrub hills pass behind JEAN, with the gold sun lower every time. His head, collar and sunglasses never move between cuts.
beats.sound: The wind roar cut hard three times, each cut landing on a different snatch of her laugh.

beats.picture: Phone frame, the sun low behind the car. Her thumb slides across the glass to the flip-camera icon in the corner, rests on it, then slides away. The lens stays on JEAN's turned head, and the frame shakes as she laughs. [Fallback: the screen flips to the front camera for under a second and catches both of them, her face cut off by the top edge, his head slumped against the door, sunglasses crooked; then it flips back to him.]
beats.sound: Wind on the mic. Her laugh, shorter.

beats.picture: Blue dusk inside the phone frame. From here the phone records without a break until it rises again at 52 s. The phone's small video light switches on and hits JEAN's black collar, and the fine desert dust on the fabric glints. His head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: The wind easing on the mic; tires on grit underneath.

beats.picture: For the first 0.8 s (19 frames) the upright phone frame still holds JEAN's turned head, and the timer runs on from REC 01:04:37, shown on these frames only. Then she lowers the phone to her lap and the picture opens to full width, film grain replacing the phone's compression: the open two-seater alone on the dusk road, VENUS laughing at the wheel with her eyes on JEAN, whose head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: For 0.8 s, wind on the phone mic. Then the wind drops away: tires and engine heard from outside the car, her laugh further off.

beats.picture: Full width, the car still moving. VENUS lifts the sunglasses off JEAN's face and, still holding them, turns his chin toward her with two fingers; his face stays turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. His eyes are open, pale and dusted. The wind moves his hair, and they do not blink. [Fallback, A16: the same action with the car parked at the motel.]
beats.sound: Tires and engine. No laugh.

beats.picture: In the first second she hooks one open arm of the sunglasses into her neckline. At 52 s she raises the phone from the driver's seat and the picture narrows back to the upright frame, with the timer showing again from that moment. JEAN's open eyes sit frontal and centered under the video light, his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. The frame shakes as she laughs. Her thumb goes to the flip-camera icon, rests there, then slides back. [Fallback: the front camera for under a second, her face lit by the video light beside his open eyes, which look past the lens; then it flips back to him.]
beats.sound: The wind comes back on the mic. Her laugh, softer and close.

beats.picture: Full width, last light. The two-seater stands in the carport of an abandoned motel under a peeling MOTEL sign on steel legs, JEAN in the passenger seat, his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. VENUS leans across his knees, into his open gaze, opens the glovebox, takes out a pistol and slides it into her back pocket. [Fallback: the pistol already in her back pocket, no hand on it.]
beats.sound: The cooling engine pinging, the glovebox latch dropping open, wind in dry palms.

beats.picture: Full width: VENUS walks the gutted motel frontage alone, the pistol grip showing from her back pocket. She tugs the padlock on the office door and looks down at the unbroken dust on its step.
beats.sound: Gravel under her boots, a loose panel on the sign ticking in the wind, the padlock knocking on its hasp.

beats.picture: At the car, VENUS lifts out his black bag, her own bag and two paper grocery sacks. JEAN stays in the passenger seat, his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it; the seat is empty now. She carries the bags to a ground-floor room and shoulders its swollen door open.

beats.picture: Inside the room: one battery lantern on a wooden table, a bedroll on the floor and a row of empty water jugs along the far wall. Her hands set down cans, full water jugs, oranges and a palm-sized photo printer, then pull a second chair up to the table. On the wall above are dozens of long-lens photos of JEAN, alone in every one; none show the two of them together.
beats.sound: The lantern switch clicking, cans set down on wood, a chair leg dragging across the boards.

beats.picture: A held frame in which nothing moves: the lantern, the oranges, the cans, the printer, two empty chairs, the bedroll and the row of empty jugs along the far wall. Above the table is the wall of JEAN photos, none of which include her.

beats.picture: The same held frame of the lantern-lit table, the two empty chairs, the bedroll and the wall of JEAN photos, with the LIMERENCE title card landing over it.
beats.sound: Silence.

script.idea_in_one_line: Her phone keeps recording a man who never wakes; his open eyes show why, and her thumb won't turn the camera on herself.

beats.picture: The upright phone frame fills the screen. Stopped at the stop sign, VENUS's hand brushes dust off JEAN's black shirt and straightens his collar while his head stays turned to the door.

beats.picture: Blue dusk, the full-width shot reframed upright. VENUS lifts the sunglasses off JEAN's face and turns his chin toward her with two fingers, the dusk road behind them.
beats.sound: Tires on grit and the engine, heard from outside the car.

beats.picture: Phone frame under the small video light: JEAN's eyes, open, pale and dusted, fill the frame. The wind moves his hair, and they do not blink.
beats.sound: Wind on the mic.

beats.picture: Her laugh shakes the phone frame from side to side while JEAN's open eyes stay centered in it, unblinking, the timer still running.
beats.sound: Her laugh, soft and close to the mic.

cast.role: Principal. A vigilante who watches unpunished men for months, then plays decorum with them over a date. She films everything and is never in her own frame. V01 objective: get JEAN to look back at her through her phone. Pilot want: one true thing about love from him, then one photograph with him. Obstacle: he is the man she is sentencing, he answers with lines, and by the cold open he is dead. Change: from never being in his frame to the first photo of them together (SC18), while the wall moves on to the next man. Age 30-38, target 34. Every face reads 30+ at the bar (alcohol, no market code given), and she is old enough to have kept a wall for months and paid for the white apartment. Defaults: I keep Lucas's height, slimness and long brown hair with highlights. I break the genre default (a glossy femme fatale in her late 20s) and the generator's stock face (symmetrical, poreless, smiling at the lens) with pores, laugh lines, one higher brow and marked working hands. She smiles at him, never at us, until SC18. Heritage: Black American, recorded here and never put in a prompt. It is a casting choice, not a story need, and Lucas approves it (see blockers).
cast.presence: In one frame (in the left-hand-drive car the script now places): a woman in her mid-thirties, left hand on the wheel, right hand holding a phone out toward the man on her right. Her shoulders are loose and her eyes are on him, not the road. The read: in love, not driving. Her hands lead (taste note: hands before faces). At the stop sign her left hand crosses to his collar, brushes the dust off and straightens it. Her right thumb rests on the flip icon, then slides away. At the motel she leans across his knees into his open gaze and doesn't look away. She handles things slowly, and whatever she puts down lands square: cans, his shoes on the white mat, the two glasses, his folded clothes, the pink cloth. Between actions she is still and watching. She laughs with her whole torso, so the phone shakes. At the bar she sits turned fully to him, elbows off the counter, one fingertip on the straws. In the rideshare she keeps the back of her head to the dash cam, even while laughing against his mouth. In SC14 she never looks down at the drops. In SC17 she finds them herself.

cast.role: Principal. St. Jean, called J: a serial dater three nights into drinking over a breakup. His ex's domestic-violence report ended with no charges filed (A02; the case is fictional). Bar objective: win the game and take her home. Apartment objective: get her to the bedroom. Want: to stay the wronged man in her eyes and win the night. Obstacle: every lie costs him a straw, and she already knows the answers. Change: from alive to dead, and from trying to frame the two of them himself (SC08) to being framed with her once he can no longer look (SC18). In V01 his job is to be carried: dead weight, with the one face shot at 42 s. Age 34-42, target 38. Lines and a thickening waist show the charm is older than the looks it was built on. This breaks the category default (a sculpted late-20s leading man) and the generator's drift toward young and symmetrical, so his 'hit list' swagger reads as habit. Heritage: Haitian-American, recorded here and never put in a prompt. The reason is the name St. Jean and the family D01 can give him. He is Black like VENUS so the killing doesn't read as a cross-racial story the pilot isn't telling. Lucas confirms this with S01 and V02 in view (see blockers).
cast.presence: In one frame (V01): a big man in black in the passenger seat, cheek on the headrest, head turned to the door and away from her camera, so only his left jaw, ear, neck and collar show. Nothing moves but his hair, and he could be asleep. After her fingers turn his head (V01-B07), his face stays turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it, through the motel and at the table. Alive, in SC04 he sits with his shoulders rounded over the glass, elbow planted, packed duffel under the stool: a man drinking to be left alone. When she speaks he props himself up, turns his stool to her, pulls the candle over and keeps his eyes on hers. His hands join her game: a straw stood upright in the wax for himself, his phone held out to fit them both, a reach for the chimney as a trophy. In the rideshare his hands go inside her jacket for the pocket. From the lobby on, his eyes go to price and surfaces (the marble, the white room) before they go to her. He checks his teeth before he deals with the blood. At the threshold he stops half a step at the drops, then steps over them.

cast.role: Supporting, one line. Works the dive bar's Thursday late shift. Objective: close JEAN's tab and clear the counter before last call. What only he does: his tab slip sends VENUS in (SC04), and the order goes through him. Age 46-54, target 50: well past 30 for the alcohol rule, and twelve years older than JEAN. Both onlookers are men because the script calls each 'him' or 'he'. Heritage: Mexican-American, recorded here and never put in a prompt. It is a casting choice, not a story need: the two onlookers are cast apart from each other and from the leads, so no heritage is tied to one job.
